articles.title: Apple’s latest sci-fi series Pluribus luxuriates in its mystery
articles.summary: Pluribus is the new show from Breaking Bad creator Vince Gilligan, and it starts streaming on Apple TV on November 7th.
articles.body: Toward the end of the first episode of Pluribus, Carol (Rhea Seehorn), a woman put in a bizarre and impossible scenario, asks a very straightforward question: “What the fuck is happening?” It’s something you’ll likely be asking yourself a lot while watching. I certainly did. But that ongoing sense of mystery, and the measured pace with which Pluribus reveals itself, is one of the best parts of the new series from Breaking Bad creator Vince Gilligan. I can’t tell you a lot about Pluribus just yet — but I can tell you that being bewildered is part of the appeal. Okay, so what can I tell you? Carol is a successful writer of fantasy novels — excuse me, “speculative historical romance literature” — and she hates both her work and her audience. She wants to do something more meaningful, but the money she rakes in from her books makes it hard to make the switch. Despite being rich and successful, and having a caring partner who doubles as her very capable manager (Miriam Shor), Carol is mostly miserable, though she’s largely able to fake it in public. --- Join me for some spoiler-heavy discussion on November 10th While I did my best to keep this early review as free of spoilers as possible, Pluribus is really a show that begs for a deeper discussion. But I’ll need your help. So check back on The Verge on Monday, November 10th, after the first two episodes premiere and you’ve had a chance to watch, when I’ll be hosting a book club-style chat for Verge subscribers, where we can all talk about Apple’s latest foray into sci-fi. --- But all that changes when… something happens. I don’t want to get too deep into spoilers before the show premieres (the first two episodes are streaming on November 7th), but the conceit of Pluribus is that following a global event that is almost apocalyptic in nature, nearly every person on Earth is inflicted with a dose of unyielding happiness. They become peaceful and collaborative and unable to cause harm to any living thing. Carol remains unaffected — but not for a lack of trying. Early on, when she’s outside of a hospital that looks like a warzone, the “others” — which is what I’ll call these happy folks for now — try to bring her over to their side. When it doesn’t work and she freaks out, they all say in unison, “We just want to help, Carol!” [Image: It’s extremely creepy and puts Carol in a difficult position. Normally she just complains about everything wrong with the world, but now she’s just about the only person who can actually save it. Of course, how she goes about that isn’t so easy to figure out. One person up against a few billion puts her at a serious disadvantage. The thing is, while the others want Carol to be a part of their group, they also are willing to do seemingly anything to make her happy. It’s part of their nature; in fact, when Carol gets really upset or angry, it actually physically harms them. This creates a fascinating tension as she has to regulate her emotions while going through an unimaginably stressful situation. There’s a lot going on, and the first two episodes are mostly about Carol coming to grips with the bizarre situation. Which is good, because it gives viewers time to come to grips with it as well. While Pluribus has some of the energy of a post-apocalyptic story, it’s also completely unlike them in many ways. Because, really, does this world actually need saving? No one in The Walking Dead wants to be a flesh-eating zombie. But turning into a perpetually chipper person? Well, that might not be so bad. As one of the others says early on, the day the change happened was the “greatest day in the history of humanity,” and it’s not impossible to understand why some might agree, even if Carol certainly doesn’t. Pluribus really digs into the nitty-gritty of how this new and very unique world works, and it isn’t afraid to take its time doing so. There’s a level of trust that Gilligan and his team have put into the show’s structure. “The older I get, the more confident I get, not in terms of my abilities but in the wisdom of the audience,” Gilligan told me ahead of the premiere. “The kind of shows that we create attract really smart viewers.” [Image: That’s why there are long, often dialogue-free sequences depicting, say, a woman getting on a plane and flying halfway around the world. You don’t know why she’s doing it at all initially, or even who she is, but the show rewards your patience. The same goes for seemingly boring practical details like how food production works in a world where most of humanity is incapable of harming any living creature. These aspects of the story provide some of the most impactful — and occasionally disturbing — revelations. Pluribus has a strange premise, but the show’s creators also think it through to its logical conclusion (at least that’s true early on; I haven’t seen the whole season yet). This slow drip of reveals and information is absorbing because Pluribus is such a well-executed show. This is especially true when it comes to Seehorn’s performance, which anchors the whole thing. Carol is not a typical heroic character; she’s a miserable and often frustrating character, and yet it’s hard to keep your eyes off of Seehorn, who makes you laugh, cry, and want to wring her neck, often all at the same time. Which means that while those “What the fuck?” moments are common, they’re not frustrating like they can be in similar shows. (Sorry, Lost.) The reveals aren’t gotcha moments. Pluribus isn’t a puzzle box meant to be solved. It’s a story with a lot of strange and complicated things to share with you — and it’s more than comfortable taking its time doing just that. The first two episodes of Pluribus are streaming on Apple TV on November 7th.

articles.title: In a big year for horror, Widow’s Bay still stands apart
articles.summary: With Backrooms and Obsession, 2026 has been a great year for horror, but there’s nothing like Widow’s Bay on Apple TV.
articles.body: Horror is having a moment. In 2026, the genre is especially well-represented: new blood is dominating the box office through films like Backrooms and Obsession, established names like Sam Raimi and Damian McCarthy are at the top of their game, and long-running franchises like 28 Years Later and Resident Evil continue to stay relevant. But the most impressive piece of horror this year might just be found in the world of TV comedy: Widow’s Bay, a series that manages the delicate balance of mixing scares with laughs, while also doubling as a loving tribute to the genre. It’s the kind of combination that often doesn’t work, which is part of what makes the show so remarkable. Widow’s Bay just wrapped up its first season — a second has already been confirmed — and it tells a story that at first sounds incredibly derivative. It takes place on an isolated island in New England, which has a sordid history due to what the locals believe is a curse. In the first episode, a terrifying fog rolls into town, suggesting that a powerful evil is waking up again. Cue the Stephen King comparisons. But it’s not long before Widow’s Bay’s distinct brand of horror / comedy makes itself clear. The show is largely centered on the island’s hapless mayor, Tom (Matthew Rhys), who has a misguided desire to turn Widow’s Bay into a tourist destination that can rival Martha’s Vineyard and Cape Cod. This, of course, runs counter to the whole curse thing. And the incoming fog is just the first sign that things are not going to go well for him and his plan, though Tom ignores the signs at every opportunity. [Image: What makes the show work is that, at its core, it’s just a really scary and tense story. From the very first episode, when Tom is stressing out about a visiting travel writer from The New York Times, there’s a steadily rising sense of dread: a tour through the island’s history that’s full of stories of death and, uh, cannibalism; a calendar about wolves that for some reason also has car crash photos; a ferry captain who says simply “bad things happen here.” The show makes you feel as uneasy as the island’s residents. That sensation only grows over the course of the season, as each episode explores a different horror genre while building on the cursed lore of the island. The second episode takes place in a clearly haunted hotel, complete with a killer clown; later there’s a demonic party planning book that leads to a terrifying and unsettling beach gathering. Tom’s assistant Patricia (Kate O’Flynn) gets hunted by a Jason Voorhees–style slasher villain, and there’s even a darkly inventive take on a drug trip sequence, complete with jarring time skips. It’s because it’s such a well-crafted horror story that the comedy in Widow’s Bay hits so hard. It’s not the easiest genre mix to pull off, as creator and showrunner Katie Dippold — who knows a thing about how funny horror can be — told me ahead of the show’s premiere in April. “It can be a great combo, but it can also be a bad combo,” she explained, noting that projects that successfully blend the two genres are “few and far between.” As if to prove her point, the new Scary Movie released this month was entirely toothless. But unlike more overt attempts at infusing horror with comedy, most of the gags in Widow’s Bay are comparatively subtle — and scary in their own way. When Tom is looking through a collection of board games at the local inn, he finds one simply called Teeth; inside, there’s nothing but a pair of pliers. When Patricia finally kills the “boogeyman” who has been stalking her, she keeps her shotgun trained on his corpse at all times — from the ambulance to cremation — just in case. Even the episode titles can be hilarious. The finale, where just about everything goes wrong, is called “We hope you enjoyed your time!” [Image: This means that the jokes not only fit into the eerie nature of the world, they actually heighten it. And that was the goal all along. “I never wanted to have a moment where something scary happens and the characters don’t react truthfully,” Dippold told me. “If you’re truthful, then eventually you’ll find the comedy. That was the very hard rule.” This all comes to a head as the show wrapped up its first season. Leading into the finale, Tom was put in an impossible situation, forced to choose whether to kill his adorably inept secretary Ruth (K Callan) in order to end the curse for good, or doom the island by not acting. In the last episode, with the town’s residents and tourists stuck in a shelter due to a destructive storm, Tom finds himself in Ruth’s house, and it’s genuinely painful watching him try to decide the right path. But amidst all of this tension, there are still funny bits, like Ruth casually noting that an old boyfriend “got bit by an animal and became that animal,” or a cheerful instructional video on ritual sacrifice. And this being Widow’s Bay, things are a bit more complex than they appear, leaving Tom with an even more difficult task in front of him. You don’t just have to take my word for it. Guillermo del Toro recently called the series “hands down one of the most mesmerizing acts of narrative prestidigitation in horror.” That’s some high praise. But so is the fact that Widow’s Bay has managed to claim its own distinct lane in such a crowded moment. The finale title turned out to be incredibly accurate: I did, in fact, enjoy my time. The first season of Widow’s Bay is streaming now on Apple TV.

articles.title: At 28, Amitabh Bachchan’s granddaughter Navya Naveli Nanda works with father Nikhil Nanda at Rs 32,500-cr Escorts Kubota; says 'I would never want to restrict my identity' beyond Bachchan-Nanda legacy
articles.summary: At 28, Navya Naveli Nanda's corporate journey began in an environment far removed from the usual image associated with her famous family - around trac.
articles.body: At 28, Navya Naveli Nanda's corporate journey began in an environment far removed from the usual image associated with her famous family - around tractors and heavy farm machinery. Today, the entrepreneur works closely alongside her father, Nikhil Nanda, Chairman and Managing Director of Escorts Kubota, the listed tractor and engineering company with a market value of roughly Rs 32,500 crore.But Navya Naveli Nanda is determined to carve out an identity beyond the Bachchan-Nanda surname. The entrepreneur, who is the daughter of Shweta Bachchan Nanda and Nikhil Nanda and granddaughter of Amitabh Bachchan and Jaya Bachchan, has been vocal about building a career and life defined by her own work.Navya Naveli Nanda on Gen ZSpeaking at the launch of Aparajita, the Hindi edition of former State Bank of India Chairperson Arundhati Bhattacharya's memoir Indomitable, Navya discussed the changing priorities of Gen Z.“Young people don’t just want profit; they want purpose,” she said, describing what she sees as a strong desire among her generation to contribute to society, women and themselves.Bhattacharya, who was also part of the conversation, dismissed the stereotype that Gen Z is entitled or unwilling to work, calling the perception “totally wrong.”Navya on the uncertainty surrounding AINavya did not claim that her generation has faced greater hardships than previous generations. Instead, she said technology has eliminated some of the challenges that earlier generations experienced, while creating new uncertainties of its own.One of the biggest concerns, she noted, is artificial intelligence and its potential impact on jobs and careers.Despite those uncertainties, Nanda believes Gen Z is developing resilience through a stronger sense of purpose. She described the commitment among young people to contributing to society as “very, very strong”.Navya Naveli Nanda on women's equalityThe entrepreneur also spoke about gender equality and how young people increasingly view men and women as equals.According to Nanda, seeing the person across the table as an equal gives young women greater confidence to express their opinions. However, she acknowledged that stereotypes and structural barriers continue to exist.For her, gender equality should not simply mean women trying to catch up with men.“I think it’s about creating our own blueprint,” she said, referring to how women should be able to decide how they want to live and contribute.Nanda also stressed that men have an important role to play as partners, fathers and brothers in creating a more equal society.Navya Naveli Nanda on her famous surnameThe question of identity is particularly personal for Navya, who comes from two prominent Indian families.Her maternal grandparents are Amitabh Bachchan and Jaya Bachchan, while her paternal grandparents were the late industrialist Rajan Nanda and entrepreneur Ritu Nanda. Her father, Nikhil Nanda, heads Escorts Kubota, while her mother, Shweta Bachchan Nanda, is a writer and entrepreneur.During the conversation, Navya was asked how she separates her own identity from the surname she was born into and whether the legacy comes with additional pressure.Navya acknowledged the responsibility that comes with having a prominent family name.“Everyone has a surname,” she said, adding that she believes everyone has an equal responsibility to live up to that name.At the same time, she made it clear that she does not want her identity to be defined solely by her family.“I would never want to restrict my identity to just my last name,” she said, adding that she does not want to be defined only by her roles as a daughter, granddaughter, sister or friend.She said women are “far beyond those labels” and expressed her desire to build an identity through both her professional and personal life.Ritu Nanda's influence on Navya's careerAmong the women who influenced Navya's ambitions, her late grandmother Ritu Nanda holds a particularly significant place.Ritu Nanda, the eldest daughter of legendary filmmaker and actor Raj Kapoor, was an entrepreneur and businesswoman. Navya recalled growing up around her grandmother's business life and being fascinated by the excitement with which she spoke about her work.While friends would sometimes tease Navya for being so interested in business, she said her grandmother's enthusiasm made the corporate world seem like “the most exciting place imaginable.”“A lot of my dadi's ambition, a lot of her strength, a lot of what she did when she was younger and what I saw growing up,” Navya said, “has led me to be sitting here on this stage sharing that with you today.”She also credited her mother, Shweta Bachchan Nanda, and grandmother Jaya Bachchan as important role models while growing up.Navya Naveli Nanda's work beyond the family businessWhile Navya works alongside her father at Escorts Kubota, her professional interests extend beyond the family business.She co-founded Aara Health, a women-focused health and wellness platform, and founded Project Naveli, a non-profit initiative focused on gender equality and creating opportunities for women.She is also co-authoring The Map, a forthcoming book from HarperCollins India that explores and challenges stereotypes surrounding Gen Z.For Nanda, the question is not whether she can escape the legacy she was born into, but how she can build something of her own while acknowledging where she comes from.“I think what has been passed around me is far more than what I might even achieve in my life,” she said.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: In 1985, Mithun Chakraborty bought this sprawling Madh Island bungalow; the lavish house has separate cottages for family members
articles.summary: Bollywood star Mithun Chakraborty has built a remarkable career after facing severe financial struggles during his early years in Mumbai. The actor, w.
articles.body: Bollywood star Mithun Chakraborty has built a remarkable career after facing severe financial struggles during his early years in Mumbai. The actor, who entered the film industry with limited means, eventually became one of the biggest stars of his generation.His debut film also earned him a National Award. Yet, Mithun Chakraborty's early days were far removed from the comfortable life he leads today. The actor has spoken about sleeping on the streets and cleaning an office to gain access to its washroom. He had also once requested an interviewer to feed him. Today, Mithun Chakraborty owns several properties across India. Among his most distinctive residences is his sprawling bungalow at Madh Island in Mumbai. The property covers nearly 1.5 acres, which is around 65,000 sq ft.In 1985, Mithun Chakraborty bought his Madh Island bungalowThe property has been part of Mithun Chakraborty's family for several decades. His younger son, Namashi Chakraborty, recently spoke about the sprawling residence and its history during a conversation with Pinkvilla. “My parents bought this house in 1985, a few months after my elder brother Mimoh was born,” Namashi Chakraborty said. The family did not immediately make the Mumbai property their permanent home. They later moved to Ooty and continued living there until 2007. After returning to Mumbai, the family began staying at the Madh Island bungalow full-time. Before that transition, the property was primarily used as a holiday home. The sprawling premises now have plenty of greenery and space for the family's 22 dogs. Gardening is also one of Mithun Chakraborty's interests. “Dad loves gardening. He often keeps himself busy doing that,” Namashi Chakraborty said.The property has separate cottages for family membersRather than housing everyone inside a single structure, the bungalow has been divided into multiple cottages. Each one serves a specific purpose or provides space for different members of the family. “There are different cottages for different family members. Both my father and grandfather believed that every kid should have their own space,” Namashi Chakraborty explained. One cottage has been converted into a gym. Another is used to accommodate guests. The cottage opposite the guest area is used by Mithun Chakraborty and his wife whenever they are in Mumbai. Another cottage functions as an office. It is also where professional conversations related to the family's film projects take place. “Dad mostly stays in Kolkata”, revealed Namashi Chakraborty. "All the film-related talks as well as script discussions happen in this office,” Namashi Chakraborty said.Mithun Chakraborty's office preserves his legacyThe office is more than just a workspace. It also contains several reminders of Mithun Chakraborty's decades-long career in cinema. One wall displays his awards, along with paintings and sketches created by fans. Other sections feature photographs of Mithun Chakraborty with prominent personalities from different stages of his life. The collection includes pictures with Kannada cinema legend Rajkumar, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Bal Thackeray. There is also a photograph capturing Mithun Chakraborty receiving the Dadasaheb Phalke Award. The property has also hosted several celebrity gatherings over the years. Its courtyard reportedly became a celebration space during the family's Diwali parties. Actors such as Dharmendra and Jeetendra have been among the guests at these celebrations.Mithun Chakraborty's sons have an in-house studioThe Madh Island residence has also evolved into a creative space for the next generation of the family. A separate cottage has been transformed into a full-fledged studio. Mithun Chakraborty's sons use the facility for filmmaking activities. They can also create different sets within the property. The arrangement allows the family to conduct several film-related activities without leaving the sprawling premises.Mithun Chakraborty's yellow Beetle was once his 'first home'Among the most unusual objects associated with the property is a yellow Volkswagen Beetle. Namashi Chakraborty described the vehicle as his father's first home in Mumbai. The car dates back to Mithun Chakraborty's difficult early period. Although it is no longer fit to be driven, the actor continues to spend money on maintaining it. “When dad came to Mumbai, he didn’t have a house to live. He spent 15 days of his life in this yellow Beetle. This was his first house. Now, it is not in a condition to be driven, yet dad spends a lot of money in its maintenance,” Namashi revealed. Namashi did not disclose how Mithun Chakraborty gained access to the vehicle during those initial days. Mithun Chakraborty has several highly awaited films, including 'Jailer 2' and 'Fauzi'.DISCLAIMER: Figures presented in this article are derived from various public sources and are considered approximate unless explicitly noted. articles.title: In 2020, Zac Efron invested money in a bushland; six years later, he is turning it into his sustainable and eco-friendly hemp home
articles.summary: Zac Efron is transforming 311 acres of bushland in New South Wales into a sustainable eco-friendly home made of hemp and biodegradable materials, collaborating with designer Joost Bakker for a green future.
articles.body: Zac Efron has been looking for a space to build a unique and sustainable version of his home, which he found in the bushlands of New South Wales. The property, located an hour from Byron Bay and spanning 311 acres, is supposed to be made entirely of hemp and other biodegradable materials found in nature. The actor, who rose to popularity for his leading role in ‘High School Musical,' has invested significant time, energy, and money into his passion project to build his own off-grid, eco-friendly dream home.Zac Efron bought the barren bushlands in 2020Australian Financial Review reported that the 38-year-old star purchased the large piece of land in New South Wales six years ago. He had invested in the bushlands to create his dream project; however, getting it off the ground took some time. Now, he is working on creating his ‘FutureCave’ with the help of the innovative Dutch-Australian designer Joost Bakker.Using internal bricks and joinery, Efron and Bakker are planning on making the entire home out of hemp. The product is stated to be sourced from a farm that is located somewhere in southern New South Wales. Not only the building itself, but a lot of the items within the home itself will be made with the use of hemp, one way or the other, including mattresses, curtains, pillows, and other similar items.The remainder of the home is also going to be made using similar natural items. According to another report shared online by Realtor.com, the project will use constructed hemp blocks, recycled oyster shells, agricultural waste, and sustainable particle boards. Efron is going all out with Bakker in planning this home, seeing as the land had been sitting there barren since he first purchased it for an undisclosed amount in 2020.Joost Bakker is quite excited to work on Zac Efron’s homeIn November last year, Bakker had taken to his Instagram and posted about how Zac Efron had asked him to work on the home and how big of an honour it all was for him. He had shared a photo of the two and wrote in the caption: “For the past year we've experimented with making hemp blocks, replacing concrete with two materials that restore the environment: hemp, possibly the best plant on earth at repairing and restoring soil health, and, of course, oysters, nature's ultimate ocean restorer. We are using the most cutting-edge technology (invented by the Romans 2000+ years ago). I want to create a building material that I hope will become mainstream one day—a material that naturally breathes, is anti-mould, is naturally fire-resistant, and improves the indoor air Zac will ultimately breathe. Big thank you to the Rennie family in Hillston, NSW, who have supported this project with their hemp (and ideas!). We are getting close now, @agrico_hillston. Also, shout-out to @shuckdontchuck. I'll keep you posted on how these blocks turn out.”Since then, he has been regularly sharing updates on his account about the project and working with Efron. In May, earlier this year, he shared that he is about to start work on his home. He wrote, "Excited to get started on Zac’s house! Especially want to thank these two legends, @main__frank, for working so hard to get this project designed and approved!”His latest update came in July, when he shared a photo with the actor, possibly in his factory or working studio, as everyone was seen wearing safety goggles and orange jackets. He wrote, “Grant Shelton from @forest1au has worked in this factory for 35 years, gaining an immeasurable amount of knowledge and skills. Turning the by-product from the sawmill on site into particle board. He and his team have used this experience to turn a crop that takes 3-4 months to harvest from a seed into an exceptional quality particle board.” He also mentioned that hemp has a lot of abilities to rejuvenate the soil and that they are excited for this project to take off.More details about Zac Efron’s homeThe outlet further shared that Efron’s home will have something called six "bedroom pods." All of the structures are going to be connected by an outdoor walkway and will also boast their own personal bathroom area, along with a rooftop garden. Efron is also planning on building a large living area on the property as well.Efron also sat down for an interview with the outlet, talking about how and why he wanted to create something like this. He shared, “I live a pretty fast-paced life and work quite a bit, so in between movies and press tours, my number one goal is always to take time for myself and rest and recharge and to be in nature as much as possible and as close to the earth as I can, and this land just feels like it's perfect for that.”In 2021, Efron also put his famous LA home on the market and has been planning on fully shifting to Australia.Zac Efron last appeared in films with ‘A Family Affair’ in 2024. He currently has two films lined up for release; however, the dates have not yet been confirmed. The films include ‘Famous’ and ‘Judgement Day’.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Mom-to-be Samantha Ruth Prabhu shares traditional baby shower pictures with hubby Raj Nidimoru; says, ‘I have always had a deep respect for our traditions’
articles.summary: Samantha Ruth Prabhu, who is expecting her first child with her husband and filmmaker Raj Nidimoru, recently gave fans a glimpse into her traditional .
articles.body: Samantha Ruth Prabhu, who is expecting her first child with her husband and filmmaker Raj Nidimoru, recently gave fans a glimpse into her traditional baby shower celebration on Monday, coinciding with Ganesh Chaturthi. The actress shared a couple of dreamy pictures from the ceremony, expressing her respect for and belief in “traditions passed down through generations.”Samantha Ruth Prabhu shares baby shower picturesSamantha Ruth Prabhu took to her Instagram handle to share pictures in which she can be seen looking beautiful in a yellow ethnic outfit, with her hair left open and minimal makeup.Speaking of her accessories, the actress chose a silver choker necklace, along with matching earrings and bangles. The pictures gave fans a glimpse of the special celebrations as Samantha and her family marked the occasion with traditional rituals.Samantha Ruth Prabhu talks about her love for traditionsThe ‘Maa Inti Bangaaram’ star also talked about her deep respect for Indian traditions and rituals. She said that while she may not understand the meaning behind every ritual, she believes there is something deeper connected to them.Her caption read, “I have always had a deep respect for our traditions. I may not understand the meaning behind every ritual, but I have always believed that there is something deeper at work... in the sound of a mantra, the energy created through chanting, and the careful way the ancient practices have been passed down through generations.”Raj Nidimoru and their family attend the celebrationSamantha’s filmmaker husband, Raj Nidimoru, was also seen taking part in the festivities. Other family members were present during the traditional ceremony as well.Ram Charan’s wife, Upasana Kamineni Konidela, reacted to the pictures and wrote, “So lovely.” Actress Krithi Shetty also dropped a red heart emoji in the comments section.For the unversed, Samantha confirmed her pregnancy during the success meet of her latest release, ‘Maa Inti Bangaaram’. The actress also revealed that she would take a maternity break after the film. The film went on to cross Rs 100 crore worldwide upon its theatrical release.Samantha Ruth Prabhu and Raj Nidimoru are said to have met for the first time during the shoot of ‘The Family Man’ Season 2. They later worked together on ‘Citadel: Honey Bunny’.Samantha tied the knot with Raj Nidimoru in December 2025.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Petrolina 131 anos: 100 vagas abertas para empreendedores | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento será realizado durante o Festival Cristão e o desfile de aniversário da cidade; inscrições são gratuitas e começam nesta terça-feira (15).
articles.summary: Petrolina abre 100 vagas para empreendedores na Vila do Empreendedorismo durante o Festival Cristão e o desfile de 131 anos da cidade; inscrições são gratuitas.
articles.body:
Vila do Empreendedor de São João começa neste sábado (7), em Petrolina — Foto: Ascom / Prefeitura de Petrolina

A Prefeitura de Petrolina , por meio da Agência Municipal de Empreendedorismo (AGE Petrolina), vai realizar duas edições da Vila do Empreendedorismo durante a programação dos 131 anos do município. Ao todo, serão disponibilizadas 100 vagas para pequenos negócios de áreas como alimentação, vestuário, decoração e artesanato.

A primeira edição será realizada durante o Festival Cristão, nos dias 17 e 18 de setembro, a partir das 18h30, na Porta do Rio. A segunda ocorrerá durante o Desfile do aniversário da cidade, no dia 21 de setembro, a partir das 18h, na Praça da Catedral. Cada evento contará com 50 empreendedores.

As inscrições serão abertas nesta terça-feira (15), a partir das 10h, de forma online e gratuita. Para participar da Vila do Empreendedorismo durante o Festival Cristão, os interessados devem se inscrever pelo link de inscrição (clique aqui).

Já para a edição realizada durante o aniversário da cidade, as inscrições devem ser feitas pelo link específico disponível clicando aqui.

Dúvidas podem ser esclarecidas pelo WhatsApp da Sala do Empreendedor da AGE, pelo telefone (87) 3983-7121, ou presencialmente na Avenida Fernando Goés, 1009, em frente ao Hotel Ibis, das 8h às 13h.

articles.title: 'Mandaadi' box office collection day 5 vs 'Sardar 2': Soori starrer collects Rs 11.25 cr; Karthi film drops 38.8%
articles.summary: Soori's 'Mandaadi' and Karthi's 'Sardar 2' continued their box office journey on Monday, September 14. The two Tamil releases saw their collections fa.
articles.body: Soori's 'Mandaadi' and Karthi's 'Sardar 2' continued their box office journey on Monday, September 14. The two Tamil releases saw their collections fall from the previous day. However, 'Mandaadi' remained well ahead of 'Sardar 2' after five days in theatres.According to Sacnilk, 'Mandaadi' recorded an India net collection of Rs 11.25 cr on Day 5. The film was screened across 3,950 shows and registered an overall occupancy of 53 percent. Monday's figure was 13.8 percent lower than its Rs 13.05 cr collection on Sunday. The film has accumulated Rs 45.85 cr in India net collections so far. Its India gross collection has reached Rs 53.63 cr. The film also earned Rs 1.25 cr from overseas markets on Day 5. Its overseas gross now stands at Rs 8.75 cr, taking the worldwide gross to Rs 62.38 cr.'Mandaadi' maintains strong run'Mandaadi' opened with Rs 4.85 cr in India net collections on September 10. The film had 2,953 shows on its opening day and recorded 32.7 percent occupancy. Its Day 2 collection climbed to Rs 6.70 cr from 2,864 shows, while occupancy increased to 44.9 percent.The film continued its upward movement on Saturday. It collected Rs 10 cr from 3,354 shows and registered 53.8 percent occupancy. Sunday delivered its highest daily collection so far. The film earned Rs 13.05 cr from 3,874 shows, with occupancy reaching 60.2 percent. Monday brought a decline, with occupancy falling to 53 percent. Still, the Rs 11.25 cr net collection was higher than the film's earnings on its first three days.Tamil version leads language-wise earningsThe Tamil version contributed Rs 9.25 cr to the Day 5 India net collection. It recorded 57 percent occupancy across 2,882 shows. The Telugu version added Rs 2 cr from 1,068 shows, with occupancy at 42.1 percent. The Tamil 2D version recorded 55.36 percent overall occupancy. Morning shows registered 38.46 percent, while afternoon shows reached 61.23 percent. Evening occupancy stood at 61 percent, followed by 59.54 percent for night shows.The Telugu 2D version recorded 38.22 percent overall occupancy. Morning shows had 22.64 percent occupancy. Afternoon shows recorded 52.09 percent, while evening and night shows registered 40.91 percent and 36.91 percent, respectively.'Mandaadi' state-wise figuresThe Day 5 gross collection for 'Mandaadi' across the reported regions stood at Rs 13.15 cr. Tamil Nadu led the contribution with Rs 9.50 cr. Andhra Pradesh and Telangana added Rs 2.40 cr, while Karnataka contributed Rs 95 lakhs. Kerala recorded Rs 20 lakhs, while the rest of India contributed Rs 10 lakhs. The film's overall India net collection has now reached Rs 45.85 cr.'Sardar 2' records Rs 1.50 crKarthi's 'Sardar 2' had a considerably quieter fifth day. According to Sacnilk, the film earned Rs 1.50 cr in India net from 2,473 shows. Its overall occupancy was 19.7 percent. The Day 5 collection represented a 38.8 percent decline from Sunday's Rs 2.45 cr. The film has so far earned Rs 13.10 cr in India net and Rs 15.35 cr in India gross collections.Its overseas gross collection increased by Rs 25 lakhs on Day 5. The overseas total has reached Rs 4.50 cr. The worldwide gross collection currently stands at Rs 19.85 cr.'Sardar 2' trails 'Mandaadi''Sardar 2' opened with Rs 4.50 cr in India net collections on September 10. It was screened across 3,950 shows and recorded 24.5 percent occupancy. The film collected Rs 2.45 cr on Day 2 from 3,361 shows, with occupancy at 19.3 percent. Its Day 3 collection stood at Rs 2.20 cr from 3,035 shows. Occupancy was 21 percent. On Sunday, the film recovered slightly and earned Rs 2.45 cr from 2,754 shows. Its occupancy reached 23.6 percent.The Tamil version earned Rs 1.10 cr on Day 5 from 1,613 shows. It recorded 20 percent occupancy. The Telugu version contributed Rs 40 lakhs from 860 shows, with occupancy at 19 percent. The Tamil 2D version registered 20.46 percent overall occupancy. Morning shows recorded 12 percent, afternoon 25.23 percent, evening 18.15 percent and night 16.77 percent.The Telugu 2D version recorded 16.97 percent overall occupancy. Its morning shows registered 14.45 percent, while afternoon shows reached 21 percent. Evening occupancy was 16.64 percent, and night shows recorded 10.91 percent.On the state-wise gross front, 'Sardar 2' collected Rs 1.75 cr on Day 5. Tamil Nadu contributed Rs 1.10 cr, followed by Andhra Pradesh and Telangana with Rs 45 lakhs. Karnataka added Rs 18 lakhs. Kerala and the rest of India contributed Rs 1 lakh each.In conclusion, after five days, 'Mandaadi' has built a sizeable lead over 'Sardar 2'.DISCLAIMER: The box office numbers and the data in this article are compiled from public and industry sources. articles.title: Eric Lahuerta, cocinero: "El truco para que las patatas bravas queden crujientes por fuera y cremosas por dentro está en la temperatura del aceite"
articles.standfirst: El chef explica cómo hacer unas patatas bravas caseras perfectas con una doble fritura y el aceite a 180 grados
articles.summary: El chef explica cómo hacer unas patatas bravas caseras perfectas con una doble fritura y el aceite a 180 grados
articles.body: Las patatas bravas son uno de los grandes clásicos de la gastronomía española, pero conseguir que queden crujientes por fuera y tiernas por dentro no depende únicamente de elegir una buena patata. La temperatura del aceite y la forma de realizar la fritura son dos de los factores que pueden marcar la diferencia entre una tapa bien hecha y unas patatas blandas o excesivamente grasas. El chef y creador de contenido Eric Lahuerta ha explicado su método para preparar unas patatas bravas caseras con una textura crujiente en el exterior y cremosa en el interior. Su principal consejo pasa por realizar una doble fritura en el mismo aceite, comenzando a baja temperatura y terminando a fuego fuerte. "El truco para conseguir unas patatas bravas crujientes por fuera y cremosas por dentro está en la temperatura del aceite", explica Lahuerta. El primer paso consiste en cortar las patatas en dados. El cocinero recomienda utilizar una variedad blanca o monalisa y, antes de llevarlas a la sartén, introducirlas en un recipiente con agua fría para eliminar parte del almidón. Este paso ayuda a evitar que las patatas se peguen entre sí durante la fritura. Después llega uno de los puntos más importantes de la técnica. Lahuerta aconseja utilizar una sartén antiadherente con aceite de oliva virgen extra y colocar las patatas directamente cuando el aceite todavía está frío. "Enciende el fuego y déjalo a fuego medio. Y directamente con el aceite en frío, añade todas las patatas", explica. La idea es que las patatas se vayan cocinando poco a poco mientras el aceite aumenta de temperatura. De esta forma, el interior se cocina antes de buscar el dorado del exterior. El momento decisivo llega cuando el aceite alcanza los 180 grados. Según el chef, entonces hay que aumentar la potencia del fuego para terminar de freír las patatas y conseguir que adquieran ese aspecto dorado y una textura crujiente. "La patata se va cocinando y en el interior va quedando bien tierna. Cuando el aceite llegue a 180 grados, va a terminar de freír la patata, dándole ese color dorado", explica. El procedimiento consiste, por tanto, en dos fases diferenciadas: primero se pochan las patatas a baja temperatura y después se fríen a fuego fuerte. "Lo que hacemos es una doble fritura en el mismo aceite. Primero, pochamos a baja temperatura, y después, freímos a fuego fuerte", señala Lahuerta. La patata es solo una parte de la receta. Para Lahuerta, la salsa también resulta fundamental para conseguir unas buenas bravas. Su preparación comienza con cebolla cortada en juliana, ajo y cayena, que deben cocinarse hasta que la cebolla quede bien caramelizada. Después incorpora un hueso de jamón y tomate cortado en dados. El hueso sirve para potenciar el sabor del sofrito. A continuación se añade un buen chorro de vino blanco y se deja reducir completamente. Cuando el vino ha reducido, el cocinero recomienda incorporar una cucharada de pimentón dulce y media de pimentón picante. El último paso consiste en añadir caldo de pollo y dejar que la mezcla cocine entre 10 y 15 minutos, hasta que el líquido reduzca y la preparación adquiera textura de salsa. Después se tritura hasta conseguir una salsa fina.

articles.title: ‘Haiwaan’ box office collections day 4: Saif Ali Khan and Akshay Kumar starrer earns less than a crore on its first Monday; India net reaches Rs 8.05 crore
articles.summary: Despite a star-studded cast, Priyadarshan's thriller ‘Haiwaan’ struggles at the box office with disappointing collections on its first Monday, earning less than a crore, raising questions about its overall performance.
articles.body: Priyadarshan’s ‘Haiwaan,’ starring Saif Ali Khan and Akshay Kumar, was released on the big screens on September 11, 2026. After the opening weekend, on its first Monday, the earnings of ‘Haiwaan’ took a nosedive. The movie made less than a crore on its day four, according to the latest box office numbers. The domestic net and gross collections missed the Rs 10 crore mark.‘Haiwaan’ box office collections on day 4 in IndiaAccording to Sacnilk, on day 4, ‘Haiwaan’ earned Rs 0.70 crore net across 3,265 shows on Monday. It represents a 62.2% drop from Sunday's net collection of Rs 1.85 crore. After a 4-day theatrical run, the net collection of ‘Haiwaan’ in India stands at Rs 8.05 crore. Further, the India total gross collection has reached Rs 9.63 crore.The movie debuted with Rs 3 crore on Friday, earned across 7,224 shows. Then came the first weekend, where, on Saturday, across 5,759 shows, the movie earned Rs 2.50 crore. On day 3, Sunday, the film made Rs 1.85 crore across 4,374 shows.‘Haiwaan’ worldwide box office collections on day 4Meanwhile, the movie earned Rs 0.25 crore on Monday in the overseas market. This has taken the overseas gross to Rs 3.00 Cr so far, pushing the worldwide gross collection to Rs 12.63 crore.‘Haiwaan’ day 4 occupancy dataThe overall occupancy recorded on day 4 was 12.88%. The day began with a 7.38% occupancy rate in the morning show, which got better during the afternoon as it rose to 14.77%. The evening shows saw a slight decline in the occupancy rate; it went down to 12.77%. Night shows saw the maximum occupancy of 16.62%.About ‘Haiwaan’‘Haiwaan’ is a thriller drama, wherein Saif Ali Khan plays the role of a visually impaired person, Shyam, an aide to a retired judge (played by Boman Irani). After the judge’s death, Shyam senses foul play, and though he can’t see, he can detect the presence of the killer (Akshay Kumar) in the room. articles.title: Telefónica acuerda con DAZN ofrecer su paquete de LaLiga: 1.650 millones por cinco temporadas
articles.standfirst: El contrato no exclusivo abarca cinco temporadas a razón de 330 millones anuales y Telefónica mentiene el 100% del fútbol de Primera División
articles.summary: El contrato no exclusivo abarca cinco temporadas a razón de 330 millones anuales y Telefónica mentiene el 100% del fútbol de Primera División
articles.body: Telefónica ha alcanzado un acuerdo con la compañía DAZN para la distribución de su paquete de LaLiga EA Sports, un acuerdo no exclusivo para 5 temporadas que asciende a 330 millones de euros de media para cada una de ellas. Dicho paquete de DAZN LaLiga incluye cinco partidos por jornada del Campeonato Nacional de Liga de Primera División, en las 38 jornadas y para su explotación en el mercado residencial, según ha apuntado Telefónica a la Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores (CNMV). Todo ello en la modalidad de pago en España (Opción D, Lote D.2). El acuerdo, suscrito el 14 de septiembre, de la mano de Telefónica Audiovisual Digital no es exclusivo y se extiende para las temporadas que van de la 2027/2028 a la 2031/2032. El valor del acuerdo asciende a 330 millones de euros de media para cada una de las temporadas. Con este acuerdo, Telefónica podrá continuar ofreciendo el 100 % de los partidos del Campeonato Nacional de LaLiga de Primera División a sus clientes, junto con la UEFA Champions League para la cual Telefónica tiene los derechos hasta 2031. Cabe recordar que el pasado mes de junio, Telefónica firmó el contrato con LaLiga que convirtió en definitiva la adjudicación previa del Lote D.1 Opción D a la compañía.

articles.title: Ester Expósito rompe su silencio y habla por primera vez de la polémica con el Xokas: "No tuve que hacer nada"
articles.standfirst: La actriz cuenta a María Guerra cómo vivió los comentarios del streamer y celebra la reacción de Burger King tras la polémica
articles.summary: La actriz cuenta a María Guerra cómo vivió los comentarios del streamer y celebra la reacción de Burger King tras la polémica
articles.body: Ester Expósito se ha pronunciado por primera vez sobre la polémica que protagonizó junto a El Xokas este verano. La actriz ha hablado con María Guerra en La Script en una entrevista en la que ha explicado cómo vivió las reacciones a los comentarios del streamer y qué conclusión sacó de todo lo ocurrido. La conversación llega después de que las declaraciones de El Xokas sobre Expósito provocaran una fuerte controversia y de que Burger King decidiera posteriormente cancelar su colaboración con el creador de contenido. El episodio comenzó cuando El Xokas habló de la actriz durante una retransmisión y aseguró que, aunque le parecía un "diez", no estaría con una mujer como ella por sus ideas políticas y que preferiría estar con una que fuera "un seis". Sus palabras generaron numerosas críticas y la polémica llegó incluso al Congreso de los Diputados. Ahora, meses después, María Guerra preguntó directamente a Expósito cómo había gestionado aquella situación. La periodista fue quien hizo referencia a las palabras del streamer y a la imagen que se había generado alrededor de ellas. La respuesta de la actriz fue clara: considera que no necesitó intervenir porque, a su juicio, las propias imágenes y declaraciones hablaban por sí solas. "No tuve que hacer nada. La situación era tan... hablaba por sí sola, la imagen, lo que decía", explica Expósito durante la entrevista. La actriz añade que para ella fue "maravilloso" que se produjera una situación en la que no tuviera que salir públicamente a responder. Más allá de las declaraciones concretas del streamer, Expósito asegura que lo que más le sorprendió de todo el episodio fue la reacción que recibió por parte de otras personas. La actriz explica que habitualmente percibe en las redes sociales mucho ruido procedente del odio, el extremismo y los comentarios misóginos. Por eso, encontrarse con una reacción diferente le sirvió para recordar que también existe otra parte de la sociedad que permanece más silenciosa. En ese momento, según cuenta, recordó que también hay "gente con dos dedos de frente" que no es misógina ni está "llena de odio, de veneno". Y considera que esa parte de la sociedad simplemente suele hacer menos ruido. "Esta gente está ahí, lo que pasa es que normalmente están calladas, tranquilas con sus vidas y los que hacen más ruido son los otros", señala. Durante la conversación con María Guerra también aparece la decisión de Burger King de poner fin a su colaboración con El Xokas. La cadena anunció el 16 de julio que cancelaba la colaboración con el creador de contenido y aseguró que sus declaraciones no representaban los valores que defendía la compañía. Sin embargo, la actriz introduce una reflexión más amplia sobre el caso. Para ella, el problema no termina con una polémica concreta ni con la reacción de una marca. "Él me puso a mí, yo era la diana en ese caso de sus declaraciones, pero ¿cuántas cosas no habrá dicho antes esta persona y tantas como él, y ahí siguen y no pasa nada? Y tienen a muchísimos oyentes y a gente que piensa como ellos", plantea. Expósito considera que habría que actuar antes cuando personas con grandes audiencias realizan este tipo de declaraciones, especialmente cuando sus mensajes pueden llegar a millones de seguidores. "A lo mejor hay que actuar antes", concluye.

articles.title: Motivational quote of the day by Lady Gaga: ‘You have a much greater mission on this earth...Your mission is to give people a form of love through your art that lifts them up,’ a powerful life lesson on kindness, purpose and inspiring others
articles.summary: Discover Lady Gaga's inspiring quote about the deeper mission of artists to spread love and kindness through their art. Explore her transformation and thoughts on creativity in today's social media age.
articles.body: Lady Gaga has always done things her own way. Her clothes, music and stage performances have helped make her instantly recognisable. But there is another side to the singer that goes beyond the costumes and the attention they receive. Gaga has often spoken about her work, her fans and the kind of feeling she wants her art to leave behind.As her career moved forward, her thoughts about fame changed too. Earlier, getting a reaction was often part of her image. Later, she began talking more about kindness and what her music could offer to someone listening. For Gaga, being an artist is not only about being noticed; it is also about having something meaningful to say. It is also about making someone feel better, stronger or less alone.Today's quote of the day by Lady Gaga reads: "You have a much greater mission on this earth than to freak the hell out of people. Your mission is to give people a form of love through your art that lifts them up."What does the quote by Lady Gaga mean?Lady Gaga offered these words in a 2019 interview with ELLE. Those experiences made her look past the shock value that had once been attached to her image.The main takeaway from Gaga’s words is simple: an audience has a responsibility. An artist can use that attention merely to entertain or can use it to leave people with something meaningful.The phrase "lifts them up," is equally important. Gaga is talking about work that leaves an audience feeling encouraged rather than diminished. Her thoughts during the interview also reflected her growing belief in kindness and the positive use of her influence.How is the quote by Lady Gaga relevant today?The thought becomes even more interesting in the age of social media. Today, attention can arrive within seconds, but keeping that attention often means competing with thousands of other voices. Controversial opinions, dramatic content and outrage can quickly become viral.For young creators, that environment can make it tempting to believe that the loudest content is always the most successful. Gaga's words suggest another possibility: creativity does not have to shock people to matter.A song might help someone get through a difficult day. A movie can make a person see their own experiences differently. A photograph, story or social media post can remind someone that their feelings are understood.That is why her words can extend beyond the entertainment industry. Students, writers, teachers, influencers and professionals also have an audience in their own spaces. What they choose to say can affect the people listening to them.Early life of Lady GagaBorn Stefani Joanne Angelina Germanotta on March 28, 1986, in New York City, Gaga showed an interest in music from a young age. Gaga took up the piano at the age of four and started writing music while she was still young. She later enrolled at New York University's Tisch School of the Arts, but decided to leave after a year and concentrate on becoming a musician. She spent the next few years performing at venues in New York and trying out different sounds and looks. It was also when she started developing the stage persona that would become known as Lady Gaga.Lady Gaga’s rise to fame'The Fame' was released in 2008 and Gaga’s name began to spread to a much wider audience. 'Just Dance' and 'Poker Face' became early favourites and helped establish her in the pop music scene. Her unusual visual style and theatrical performances made her instantly recognisable, while her music established her as one of pop's major new voices.She continued that success with The Fame Monster in 2009, which included songs such as 'Bad Romance' and 'Telephone'. Her career expanded further with albums including Born This Way, as she continued experimenting with her sound and public image.Music was eventually joined by acting. Gaga played Ally in 'A Star Is Born' with Bradley Cooper. The role brought her acting work into the spotlight, while 'Shallow' took home the Academy Award for Best Original Song.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: 2026 Emmy Awards: Winners and losers
articles.summary: Matthew Rhys made Emmy Awards history by winning two lead acting awards in one ceremony, but the full list of winners holds even more surprises.
articles.body: The 78th Emmy Awards took place Monday night at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, with Mariska Hargitay hosting the ceremony – the first woman to host the award show in 15 years. "The Pitt" led all programs with 25 nominations, while "Hacks" earned a record 24 nominations during its final season. Apple TV’s "Widow’s Bay" followed with 19 nominations, and "Pluribus" had 18. The Creative Arts Emmys were presented ahead of Monday night, with notable wins for Shailene Woodley, Mariska Hargitay, Bad Bunny and the late Rob Reiner. "Widow’s Bay" led the early awards with eight wins, while "DTF St. Louis" earned six. Matthew Rhys made Emmy history Monday night by winning two lead acting awards in the same ceremony. The actor first won outstanding lead actor in a limited or anthology series for Netflix’s "The Beast in Me" before taking home outstanding lead actor in a comedy series for Apple TV’s "Widow’s Bay." articles.title: Shah Rukh Khan confirms 'King' release is NOT delayed, says he suffered a few injuries while shooting: 'All broken is fixed'
articles.summary: Amid speculation that Shah Rukh Khan’s much-awaited film ‘King’ could be pushed from its scheduled release date, the superstar has put the rumours to .
articles.body: Amid speculation that Shah Rukh Khan’s much-awaited film ‘King’ could be pushed from its scheduled release date, the superstar has put the rumours to rest. During an ‘Ask Me Anything’ session on X (formerly Twitter) on Tuesday, SRK confirmed that the film is on track and will arrive in theatres on December 24, 2026, as planned.A fan seeking an update on the film wrote, “Sir KING ka kuch update do….3 saal pehle last movie dekhi thi aapki theaters mein…aur kitna tarsao ge ek trailer ke liye hi?" Responding to the query, Shah Rukh said, “Ab picture hi dekho na! Tarsa nahi raha join acchhi wali bana raha hoon….ke Dil ko tasalli mile….Sab ayega…24th Dec se pehle."The actor also opened up about the challenges he faced while filming ‘King’. Replying to another user, SRK revealed that he sustained multiple injuries during the shoot, which led to the schedule being stopped and restarted several times. “Had a few injuries while shooting so had to start stop many times but now all broken is fixed…and nearly all done…so all good," he wrote.When asked what audiences could expect from the film, Shah Rukh highlighted the various elements he has worked on, including his look. “Everything in #King …worked very hard to entertain as many as possible. The action the songs the actors and of course my hair!!!" he said.Directed by Siddharth Anand, ‘King’ is an action thriller and has been among the most anticipated Bollywood releases. The film marks Shah Rukh’s return to the big screen after ‘Dunki’ and also features his daughter Suhana Khan in a key role. Deepika Padukone and Abhishek Bachchan are also part of the ensemble cast.
